newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch cargo industry and Customs boost cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch cargo industry and Customs boost cooperation.

text.p: ATAN, the Netherlands air transport association, said it has signed a preliminary agreement with the Dutch customs authority designed to facilitate closer co-operation between the two organisations.
ATAN spokesman Hans Knuvers said the memorandum of understanding meant that ATAN would deliver information faster to the customs authority.
"We are (also) aiming to encourage the individual ATAN members to inform customs officials if they are aware of anything suspicious," he added.
The understanding would enable the customs authority to have more efficient controls and to speed up the information process between the freight industry and customs, he added.
NVLA, NVVL, DATA, DAGSA and ACAN -- respectively the Netherlands handlers', forwarders', truckers', general sales agents' and air cargo carriers' associations -- are all members of ATAN.
"ATAN hopes to encourage them all to sign individual agreements with the customs authority," said Knuvers.
Dutch customs would then be able to put more energy into its fight against drugs, weapons traffic and illegally copied items, he said.
However, the agreement would also help avoid logistical bottlenecks, as the two parties aimed to speed up and make control processes more efficient through Amsterdam Schiphol airport, he added.
